_comment: Enemy roster. SIX types in version one: Sweepers, Stockers, Glimmers, WindowWalkers, Ficus, Warden. Every enemy must telegraph with sound before sight - that is an accessibility requirement, not polish.
_scopeNote: History of this line, because it has moved twice and both moves were approvals rather than drift. It read 'four types' until the edit that added WindowWalkers deleted it; Chris approved that fifth type on 2026-10-20. Codex added the ficus concept art and Chris approved it the same day ('Codex did it, I like the ficus'), making six. A seventh needs his approval the same way. The rule is not the number - it is that a guardrail moves deliberately and never gets removed by whoever needs it out of the way.
_ficusTodo: APPROVED but NOT DEFINED. Concept art is at assets/enemies/ficus-stalker-concept-v1.png; there is no entry for it below and no rig. A mall local per docs/ZONES.md, like the WindowWalkers - derived from mall landscaping. Its stats are Chris's call, as all values in this file are.

Sweepers.behaviour: Weak alone. Swarm lit players and dropped loot.
Sweepers.counterplay: Kill lights, move, or drop loot as a decoy.

Stockers.behaviour: Slow, tall, strong line of sight.
Stockers.counterplay: Break sight and pass in darkness.

Glimmers.behaviour: Complete a 2-second scan, then tag one player for 20 seconds.
Glimmers.counterplay: Go dark before the scan completes; break sight and relocate if tagged.

WindowWalkers.behaviour: Remain still until a nearby active lantern catches them, then walk directly after the light source.
WindowWalkers.counterplay: Go dark and break sight; they do not navigate around a lost target.

Ficus.behaviour: Stands as a potted plant until lantern light catches it, then creeps after the light source.
Ficus.counterplay: Go dark, break sight, and do not light every decorative plant in a department store.

Warden.behaviour: Converges on the brightest position once the Warden's own arrival meter fills - see storm-charge.json `warden`, which Chris split out of the generic thresholds on 2026-10-28. It is a late-night escalation, not the normal consequence of using a lantern. Brightest position, never nearest player: that is what puts cause and consequence in the same pair of hands.
Warden.counterplay: Hide, kite, distract, or extract. Never kill it.
Warden._comment: Not a boss. It is Storm Charge's final warning given a body. If it ever becomes killable, the meter stops meaning anything.
